title: All 200 HadSST4 bias-adjustment members retain a rising west-minus-east Pacific temperature contrast in 1982-2022
abstract: We tested whether bias-adjustment uncertainty changes the Pacific sea-temperature trend pattern. We used all 200 HadSST.4.2.0.0 members, the median grid and the unadjusted grid on matched available five-degree cells. In 1982-2022, the west-minus-east equatorial Pacific trend is 0.1504 to 0.1680 degrees C per decade across the full ensemble. The unadjusted trend is 0.1797. The east-Pacific trend changes from -0.0442 in unadjusted data to an ensemble median of -0.0013, with a range of -0.0100 to 0.0092. Thus absolute cooling and the regional contrast have different sensitivity to the adjustments. The east and west trend errors have a correlation of 0.725 across members. Treating them as independent would change the contrast standard deviation from 0.0031 to 0.0060. The conditional 24-month residual interval for the gradient is -0.0151 to +0.3311 degrees C per decade and includes zero. These intervals concern an underlying stochastic trend, not measurement error of the realized slope. The results constrain the represented bias choices only. Gaps, common errors, measurement uncertainty and climate variability limit the result.

display.caption: Full bias-ensemble ranges and conditional time-series intervals. Unadjusted data diagnose the applied corrections; they are not a preferred estimate of climate change.

citations.reason: Extends the matched-coverage study to the full bias-adjustment ensemble and its covariance. No source code or monthly extracts were reused.
Tests the regional contrast and qualifies the absolute east-Pacific cooling statement within one in situ product.
The surviving model-observation pattern gap motivates a test of reference-product bias uncertainty. We do not rerun its model comparison.
